original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Replace repeated scalar label parity counts by exact incidence bitsets in the complete P104 span-fact command; measure its complete enclosing bounded verifier with all inherited checks retained.
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card permits one profiled stage; this package optimizes the complete retained PR6188 span-fact command and measures its enclosing bounded verifier.
bottleneck_link: The profiled S0 loop dominates the span-fact command. Retaining its complete caller makes the measured gain relevant to the bounded B-form replay.
stop_rule: Ship the first verified complete-command improvement; stop after the incidence substitution. Do not optimize the other replay stages.
evidence: PROOF.md, verify.py and the generated BENCHMARK.json record the scoped equivalence, complete output comparisons and timings.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can the same source-bound incidence representation help another explicit finite-fact consumer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Further gains require a measured consumer; this package changes only the S0 stage.
open_questions.first_step: Profile a different complete command and specify its full retained output and checks before implementing reuse.
open_questions.blocked_by: No other consumer is measured or adapted here.
